title: AMD Forecasts Over 80% Revenue Growth in 2027 as Data Centers Top 80% of Sales

tickers.name: Meta Platforms, Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
AMD CEO Lisa Su projected on the company's third quarter earnings call that total revenue will grow more than 80% in 2027, more than double the long term target set last November, with data centers expanding to over 80% of company sales from 64% in the third quarter. Full year 2026 data center revenue will more than double from 2025, while server CPU revenue will double in 2027, up from an earlier forecast of over 70% growth. In contrast, the company plans for a double digit decline in PC market unit shipments in 2027 alongside double digit growth in its embedded segment.

AMD began revenue shipments of its next generation EPYC Venice server processors in the third quarter, securing commitments from hardware partners for more than 240 platforms, 20% above the prior Turin generation. OpenAI also selected EPYC Turin as the host CPU for its first custom AI accelerator platforms, while Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure are running workloads on the first AMD Helios rack scale systems powered by MI450 GPUs. In addition, Vultr will deploy Helios systems built by HPE in a $12B deal, and AMD is working with frontier AI labs to optimize upcoming MI500 accelerators for multi gigawatt deployments.

The call followed AMD's third quarter report showing revenue rose 45% from a year earlier to $13.38B and adjusted earnings reached $2.09 a share, driven by a 97% jump in data center revenue to $8.55B. For the fourth quarter, AMD forecast revenue of about $17B, plus or minus 3%, and adjusted gross margin of roughly 55%, down from 56% in the third quarter. Third quarter GAAP net income of $2.43B included a $1.1B non cash charge from revaluing customer warrants granted to OpenAI and Meta to buy up to 320 million combined shares at $0.01 each, reducing GAAP earnings by $0.66 a share. AMD shares rose more than 9% in after hours trading.

$AMD CEO Lisa Su:

“We now expect revenue to grow more than 80% in 2027,” more than twice the company's long-term growth target outlined last November.

Data Center is now expected to account for over 80% of AMD's total revenue in 2027, up from 64% in Q3.

Server CPU revenue is expected to double YoY in 2027, compared with the previous forecast of 70%+ growth.

Data Center AI revenue is expected to grow even faster than management projected just 90 days ago.

Su said customers have expanded their EPYC and Instinct deployment plans, while AMD has secured additional supply to support the higher growth outlook.

Looking beyond 2027, AMD is also working with multiple frontier AI labs to optimize its upcoming MI500 accelerators for their planned multi-gigawatt deployments.

selectedTweets.bestBit: AMD guided Q4 adjusted gross margin to about 55%, down from 56% in Q3, as lower-margin AI racks become a bigger part of sales.
selectedTweets.text:
AMD $AMD JUST GUIDED TO $17.0B IN Q4 REVENUE, WELL ABOVE THE $16.2B WALL STREET EXPECTED

That's +66% from a year ago and a +27% jump from Q3 in a single quarter.

It also lands exactly on the number Jefferies was modeling heading into tonight, the high end of the range on the Street.

AMD said it expects "growth to accelerate further in the fourth quarter as we scale Helios and 'Venice' production." Helios is its new AI server rack, and Venice is its next-generation EPYC server chip.

The one give-back is margins. AMD guided Q4 adjusted gross margin to about 55%, down from 56% in Q3, as lower-margin AI racks become a bigger part of sales.

This is AMD's 9th straight quarter beating revenue estimates.

selectedTweets.bestBit: Buried in AMD's Q3 earnings reconciliation is a $1.097B change in the fair value of customer warrants, reducing GAAP EPS by $0.66.
selectedTweets.text:
$AMD RECORDED A $1.1B NON-CASH CHARGE TIED TO ITS OPENAI & META WARRANTS DEALS IN Q3

Buried in AMD's Q3 earnings reconciliation is a $1.097B change in the fair value of customer warrants, reducing GAAP EPS by $0.66.

Here's how it works.

Under its AI deals, OpenAI and Meta each received warrants to buy up to 160 million AMD shares at just $0.01 per share, or 320 million shares combined.

The warrants vest as customers meet GPU purchase commitments and AMD achieves specified stock-price milestones.

AMD must revalue these warrants every quarter based on its stock price and other assumptions. As their value increases, AMD records an accounting expense.

So the $1.1B charge wasn't cash paid to customers, but it was the largest single adjustment between AMD's $2.43B GAAP net income and $3.47B adjusted net income.

The other thing worth watching is the potential shareholder dilution if those warrants eventually vest and are exercised.
